title: nebula-analytics-private-deploy-acceptance-and-upgrade-checklist
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Nebula Analytics private deployment (VPC + on-prem hybrid). It combines a sizing proposal, Terraform module notes, acceptance criteria for a staged upgrade, and an operational cutover checklist. Target audience: solutions engineering, infra team, and customer ops for Nebula Analytics.

Executive summary:
- Customer profile: Nebula Analytics, mid-market SaaS with bursty inference (batch ETL + interactive analyst queries). Peak expected inference traffic: 1,200 concurrent sessions during business hours, plus nightly batch of 6M tokens/hour.
- Goal: Provide a predictable on-prem + VPC deployment that meets 250ms median token latency for interactive queries, supports nightly batch throughput, and allows zero-downtime model upgrades with rollback.
- Proposed capacity (initial): 4 x H100-style nodes (3x active + 1x hot spare) for async/batch, 6 x A100/A10G mixed nodes for interactive low-latency workloads behind autoscaler. This is intentionally conservative for first 90 days.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Average interactive request length: 160 tokens input, 80 tokens output. Average tokens per interactive session: 240.
- Batch jobs: average sequence length 2048, highly parallelized.
- Quantized model variant available (4-bit) reduces memory footprint by ~2.5x vs fp16.
- Customer network: 10Gbps uplink between on-prem cluster and customer VPC peering, MTU 1500.
- Storage: model artifacts stored in S3-compatible object store accessible from both control plane and worker nodes.
- KMS: customer will provide key material via AWS KMS or on-prem HSM; RBAC enforced via Vault token exchange.
- Terraform state: remote backend in S3 with DynamoDB locking for AWS-hosted control plane modules.

Sizing rationale and quick math:
- Interactive capacity: target 1,200 concurrent sessions * 240 tokens = 288k tokens in-flight. At 80 tokens/sec per H100-ish GPU (conservative estimate depending on model/sequence), we need ~3.6 GPUs effective capacity. We provision 6 mixed nodes to allow headroom, autoscaling, and routing by SLO class.
- Batch capacity: target 6M tokens/hr = ~1.67k tokens/sec sustained. At 5k tokens/sec per H100 for batch-optimized runtimes, 1 node can handle batch load, but we propose 3 nodes to absorb spikes and provide parallelism for different models.
- Storage sizing: model cache (KV cache) per active model: ~8–12GB. Allow 200GB per GPU node for local model artifacts + logs. Central object store initial capacity 2TB with lifecycle to glacier-equivalent for older artifacts.
- Network: plan for 10Gbps interconnect as minimum; certain heavy-recall workloads may need 25Gbps.

Terraform module notes (implementation details and gotchas):
- Module naming: recommend modules/nebula-{vpc,roles,cluster,model-artifacts,monitoring,iam}. Keep module outputs minimal and stable (avoid outputting dynamic ARNs where possible).
- Providers: pin aws provider to 4.x (for provider changes see PR #68) and use cloud-native resource names with tags: "nebula:customer=nebula-analytics".
- State isolation: separate Terraform state workspaces per environment (dev/staging/prod). Avoid state workspaces per customer to prevent accidental resource collisions; instead use separate backends or prefixes for true isolation.
- Locking: enable DynamoDB table for locking; add an automated guard in CI to verify locks are in place before apply.
- Module variable hygiene: enforce explicit GPU type, disk encryption boolean, kms_key_id string, and allowed CIDR blocks. Provide reasonable defaults but require explicit approval for any change to gpu_count or instance_type.
- Migration notes: when changing cluster_size variable, ensure rolling update policy is configured so that draining/cordon occurs before termination. Use lifecycle rule create_before_destroy where applicable for ASG replacements.

Upgrade plan (staged with acceptance gates):
Phase 0: Pre-upgrade prep (non-prod)
- Apply infra changes in dev/staging workspaces.
- Run synthetic load tests using the benchmark harness in private-terraform repo.
- Validate metrics ingestion to Datadog: token latency distribution, GPU utilization, OOM counts.
Acceptance gate: no synthetic 95th latency regressions >10% and no OOMs for 2 consecutive runs.

Phase 1: Canary in prod (low traffic window)
- Provision new model variant nodes in separate AZ/subnet behind a canary routing policy. Route 2.5% of traffic to canary.
- Monitor for 2 business days: error rate, latency, cost per token, and model output quality via golden prompt set.
Acceptance gate: error rate <0.1% and quality A/B tests pass threshold (A/B quality delta < 0.5% for precision metrics).

Phase 2: Gradual rollout
- 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over multi-day windows with rollback windows after each step.
- Automate rollback to previous variant via routing policy with version pinning.
Acceptance gate: SLOs met at each step.

Phase 3: Post-upgrade validation
- Run nightly batch jobs to validate throughput. Validate cost and tracing metrics.
- Run final smoke tests and update runbooks.

Cutover checklist (operational runbook):
Pre-cutover:
- Confirm Terraform plan reviewed and approved (PR link required).
- Verify backups of Terraform state and snapshot of key storage volumes.
- Ensure on-call rotation assigned and Slack channel created (#nebula-deploy).
- Document maintenance windows and notify Nebula ops 72/24 hours ahead.
During cutover:
- Put monitored routes into canary mode.
- Monitor queue depth, latency, GPU memory pressure.
- Keep HSM/KMS credentials available and verified.
Post-cutover:
- Validate golden prompts and batch jobs.
- Run smoke test suite and tag release in internal registry.

Rollback plan (if things go wrong):
- Immediate fallback: switch routing policy to pinned previous model version (1-click via Console).
- If infrastructure issue: revert Terraform by applying previous workspace state snapshot; coordinate with infra lead to avoid drift.
- Communication: post status to #nebula-deploy and page SRE per escalation matrix.

Acceptance criteria (SLA and validation checks):
- Latency: median token latency <= 250ms for interactive median; 95th percentile < 800ms.
- Availability: >= 99.9% during business hours for interactive endpoints.
- Batch throughput: ability to sustain 6M tokens/hr with no job failures for 24-hour run.
- Resource stability: no OOMs or model load failures during acceptance tests.
- Security: all data at rest encrypted (customer KMS), audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM.

Observability and alerting recommendations:
- Metrics: per-model token/sec, tokens/in-flight, request latency histogram, GPU util/mem/temperature, disk iops, network saturation.
- Traces: attach request traces with model-version and route metadata.
- Alerts: set P99 latency alert, OOM alert, GPU temperature alert, and model load failures.
- Dashboards: per-route latency and cost-per-token broken down by model variant.

Open questions / TODOs (customer and infra):
- Confirm preferred GPU SKUs (customer procurement windows may limit to A10G only).
- Does Nebula want on-prem HSM integration or prefer cloud KMS? (impact: key rotation flow).
- Agree on retention for logs and evaluation artifacts (default 90 days; customer may request 365).
- Finalize disaster recovery RTO/RPO targets — proposed RTO 15 minutes for interactive routing.

Appendix A: Terraform variable checklist to include in PRs:
- "customer_id" (string)
- "environment" (string: dev/staging/prod)
- "gpu_instance_type" (string)
- "gpu_count" (number)
- "disk_encrypted" (bool)
- "kms_key_id" (string)
- "model_artifacts_bucket" (string)
- "peering_cidr" (string)
- "maintenance_window" (string)

Appendix B: Quick operational run commands (notes to SRE)
- model load: ./nebulactl load --model-uri s3://nebula-models/nebula-v2 --variant quant4
- drain node: ./nebulactl drain --node gpu-03 --timeout 1200
- snapshot TF state: aws s3 cp s3://nebula-tf-state/prod.tfstate ./state-snap-$(date +%F)

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to add explicit CI gate that runs the benchmark harness after every terraform apply to staging.
- Add a small script to auto-generate golden prompts from customer prompts repo for quicker QA.
- Follow up with Nebula procurement about GPU lead times (they asked about 6-week delivery for H100).

References and links:
- private-terraform repo PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-terraform/pulls
- benchmark harness: https://internal.redwood/benchmarks/nebula-harness
- recommended kernel optimizations: see internal doc KERNELS-2024-04

End of draft.
summary: Working draft playbook: sizing, terraform notes, staged upgrade plan, cutover checklist and acceptance criteria for Nebula Analytics private deployment. Contains assumptions, math, module recommendations, and open questions.
